text:
ajohnson: Heads-up — got a billing alert from the cloud: large egress from eu-west-3 overnight (~3.2 TB). Looks like artifact replication + trace exports fired together. :eyes:

maria_p: ugh. any idea which pipeline?

ajohnson: early look at storage logs shows a flood of GETs from a single IP range in us-central1 hitting our logs-bucket in eu-west-3 between 02:10-03:05 UTC. Also several multipart uploads for model-checkpoints->replica.

leo_ops: that sounds like the backfill job we kicked for the new quantized checkpoints. I thought we constrained region routing though — should have been eu-only.

dave_ops: I pulled the replication job config: `replicate:=true, target_regions=[eu-west-3, eu-north-1], route_preference=primary` — nothing to us-central1. But I see a fallback policy set on the worker image that allows cross-region when ENI fails.

ajohnson: interesting — billing lines show egress tagged to `trace-exporter-service` as well. Could be two independent things colliding.

maria_p: can someone run a quick query on logs to correlate the IPs to service accounts? Query I use: ```
# GCP logs sample
SELECT
  resource.labels.instance_id,
  protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail AS principal,
  protopayload.*
FROM `project.logs_*`
WHERE timestamp BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 12 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP()
AND resource.type = 'gcs_bucket'
AND protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp IN ('35.***.***.**')
LIMIT 100
```

leo_ops: ran a narrowed scan, principal is `service-operator@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com` and request path is `/artifacts/models/2026-03-13/*`.

dave_ops: that SA is used by the async trace export pipeline (we added artifact copying to tracing retention flow last month). Looks like a mis-scoped IAM grant allowed it to call the replication API.

ajohnson: so two root causes: (1) trace-export pipeline was performing an artifact copy as a side-effect, and (2) a fallback networking policy caused worker nodes to route to us-central1 which then proxied transfers back to eu-west-3 causing cross-region egress in billing.

maria_p: what's the immediate mitigation?

leo_ops: I've disabled the artifact-copy flag on trace-export jobs and paused the scheduled backfill. Also added a temporary egress deny for the worker subnet to us-central1.

infra-billing-bot: Billing alert: Potential one-time egress charge of ~3.2 TB (~$430) from eu-west-3 -> us-central1. Full report: https://billing.internal/reports/1767601234

ajohnson: good. next steps: 1) rollback the fallback network policy and add stricter region egress ACLs, 2) audit all services that have `storage.objects.copy` IAM, 3) add test for artifact-copy side-effects in trace-export CI.

maria_p: I'll own the IAM audit (will list principals with storage copy perms and map to services). Target: deliver findings by EOD.

leo_ops: I'll work on the network ACL changes and a short runbook to avoid cross-region fallback for storage traffic.

dave_ops: I'll file a support case with cloud provider to ensure these egress logs are granular for invoicing and request they waive anything that looks accidental.

ajohnson: thanks. can we also pin a tagging/label rule so egress lines include service: trace-export or service: artifact-backfill? That will make future triage easier.

maria_p: yes — I'll propose a label enforcement policy for storage clients.

leo_ops: quick note: if anyone needs to re-run any paused backfills, route them through the eu-only transfer worker we tested last month.

dave_ops: filing tickets: INFRA-2138 (network ACL change), INFRA-2139 (IAM audit), INFRA-2140 (trace-export config change).

ajohnson: perfect. keep this thread updated if you see any additional billing spikes. :thumbsup:
